subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should native `openclaw backup create` accept this exclude-pattern design, and if so should implicit `.backupignore` loading and external-asset semantics be part of the first merge?
rationale: The PR adds public backup CLI surface that can include or omit sensitive and restore-critical data, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security semantics.

options.title: Rework this PR into current main
options.body: Keep the native exclude feature but require explicit semantics, per-asset filtering, bounded verification, and real proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the first merge
options.body: Accept only repeatable explicit excludes and exclude-file support while deferring smart defaults and implicit ignore-file loading to a separate decision.

options.title: Replace the stale branch
options.body: Close or pause this PR and ask for a smaller replacement against current backup architecture if the conflict and safety debt are too high.

recommendation.title: Rework this PR into current main
recommendation.body: Keep the native exclude feature but require explicit semantics, per-asset filtering, bounded verification, and real proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main backup writer and CLI history makes this the best available owner for reconciling the feature with the new backup architecture.
